issues.title: Rename leaves Branch creation membership stale and recursive Branch copies the invalid history
issues.expected: A successful recursive Branch writes a complete command unit whose exact UID and member set can be reconstructed immediately for Undo.
issues.actual: Rename M1 changed Branch1's owner name from b1 to renamed-1 without rebasing its retained Branch membership. Branch M2 then succeeded and copied that invalid history into a seven-Context subtree. The prescribed counted inverse Rename M2 restored the original owner, but the cloned checkpoint still had a different owner UID/name; build_command_stacks continued to fail with 'Branch checkpoint owner is outside its creation membership.' All eight remaining counted Undo/Redo attempts reproduced that builder error before Context mutation, and their complete scratch Context-tree/state digests were unchanged.
issues.workaround: There is no safe in-phase recovery. Preserve the malformed history for diagnosis, avoid recursive Branch over a subtree containing renamed Branch history, and rely only on the observed fail-closed Undo/Redo behavior until Rename rebases recovery metadata or Branch rejects/isolates the invalid history before mutation.

issues.title: Context Import publishes a UID/name collision that blocks Rename
issues.expected: A successful Context import into a new local name must preserve a consistent identity graph so later world-local Rename can update references, or the import must reject the collision before mutation.
issues.actual: Import M1 succeeded and stored advisor1/style as import-direct with the source UID a759f597. The active Profile already had a granted Context reference with that UID and the source name task-2/advisor1/style. Rename M3 then failed with 'Context reference identity and stored target name disagree'; consequently Rename M5's planned cancel target was never created.
issues.workaround: Do not rename a Context imported under a new name when the active Profile already contains a reference with the source UID. Inspect the UID/name graph first and keep the imported Context at its initial name; no in-phase repair was attempted.
